application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A thin, isomorphic HTTP client wrapper around the WHATWG Fetch API (unjs/ofetch) that adds automatic JSON handling, retries, timeouts, hooks, baseURL/query management, and normalized errors.
application.purpose: Provide a developer-friendly, type-safe `fetch` wrapper for browsers, Node.js, workers, and edge runtimes, so applications can make HTTP calls with sensible defaults and less boilerplate than using raw `fetch`.

domains.name: HTTP Client
domains.description: The core domain: issuing HTTP requests, composing URLs, and normalizing response handling and errors.

domains.name: Request/Response Serialization
domains.description: Deciding how to serialize request bodies, how to detect the response parser from Content-Type, and how to parse responses into typed data.

domains.name: Resilience (Retry, Timeout, Abort)
domains.description: Retry policy on transient failures and retryable status codes, retry delays, request timeouts, and abort-signal handling.

domains.name: Hooks / Interceptors
domains.description: Lifecycle hooks (onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError) that let consumers observe and mutate the request/response lifecycle.

domains.name: Error Normalization
domains.description: A unified FetchError model carrying request, options, response, parsed data, and status information.

domains.name: Runtime Portability
domains.description: Selecting the underlying fetch/Headers/AbortController implementation per runtime (global fetch, node-fetch-native polyfill, keep-alive agents) and building distributable bundles.

terminology.meaning: The public client function; calling it returns the parsed response body (`_data`), while `$fetch.raw` returns the full FetchResponse.
The shared object passed to every hook, holding the request, resolved options, and (depending on phase) the response or error.
Per-request options after merging call-site options with global defaults, including a normalized `Headers` instance and merged query params.
The standard `Response` augmented with `_data`, the parsed payload produced by the client.
The normalized error thrown on network failure or 4xx/5xx status, exposing `request`, `options`, `response`, `data`, `status`/`statusCode`, and `statusText`/`statusMessage`.
How the response body should be interpreted: `json`, `text`, `blob`, `arrayBuffer`, or `stream`.
HTTP methods that carry a request body (PATCH, POST, PUT, DELETE); used to gate body serialization and to avoid unsafe automatic retries.
HTTP statuses considered transient and therefore retryable (default 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504).
URL composition inputs: a base URL prefix and query-string parameters (`params` is the deprecated alias of `query`).
Custom response-text parser; when provided it forces JSON-style parsing and replaces the default `destr` parser.
Factory that derives a new client instance with merged defaults and optional custom global options (fetch, Headers, AbortController).
Flag that suppresses throwing on 4xx/5xx statuses, returning the response instead.
Opt-in required for streaming request bodies (ReadableStream/Node Readable) when sending them over fetch.

entityAnnotations.businessMeaning: Factory for the HTTP client: binds a fetch implementation and defaults, then returns a callable `$fetch` with `.raw`, `.native`, and `.create` members.
Central failure handler: decides whether to retry (respecting retry count, retryable status codes, retry delay, and abort semantics) or to throw a normalized FetchError.
Builds the standardized error object from a failed request, formatting a `[METHOD] "url": status statusText message` message and exposing request/options/response/data/status as lazy getters.
Merges per-call options with global defaults, producing resolved options with a unified headers collection and combined query parameters.
Combines default headers with request-specific headers, with request-specific values winning, normalizing all supported header input shapes into a `Headers` object.
Invokes one or more lifecycle hooks in order, awaiting each so asynchronous hooks (e.g. token refresh) complete before the request continues.
Determines whether an HTTP method carries a body, used to gate body serialization and to disable automatic retries for unsafe methods.
Decides if a request body can be automatically JSON-stringified, excluding streams, buffers, FormData, and URLSearchParams which must be passed through untouched.
Infers the correct response parser from the response Content-Type, mapping JSON to `json`, SSE to `stream`, XML/HTML/text to `text`, and anything else to `blob`.
Node-specific fetch provider: returns the native/polyfilled fetch, optionally wrapping it with keep-alive HTTP/HTTPS agents when the `FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE` environment flag is enabled.
Manual smoke script that calls the client against a server-error endpoint and logs the outcome, exiting non-zero on failure.
Demonstrates the type-safety benefit of the client: a generic type parameter gives typed access to a nested response property from a public API.
Test helper that aborts an in-flight request via AbortController to verify that aborted calls are not retried and reject with an abort error.

applicationFacts: The project is the unjs/ofetch library; it is published as a library package rather than an end-user application.
Two entry points are shipped: `src/index` (isomorphic, uses global fetch) and `src/node` (Node.js-specific, may use node-fetch-native polyfill and keep-alive agents).
Public exports include `$fetch`/`ofetch`, `FetchError`, `createFetch`, `createNodeFetch`, and all type definitions.
Request bodies are auto-stringified for JSON-serializable payloads on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, with `content-type` and `accept` defaulted to `application/json`.
`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies are encoded via `URLSearchParams` instead of JSON.
Streaming request bodies (ReadableStream or Node Readable) are supported and automatically set `duplex: "half"`.
Responses are parsed with `destr` by default for tolerant JSON parsing; `parseResponse` allows a custom parser.
Response bodies are skipped for 101/204/205/304 statuses and for HEAD requests, yielding `undefined` data.
Automatic retries default to 1 attempt for non-payload methods and 0 for payload methods; retryable statuses are 408, 409, 425, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 and can be overridden.
Retry delay supports a fixed millisecond value or a callback receiving the fetch context.
A `timeout` option is implemented with an AbortController and a `TimeoutError` (DOMException code 23) abort reason; an explicit user-supplied signal takes precedence.
Aborted requests are not retried automatically.
Errors of status 400–599 throw a `FetchError` unless `ignoreResponseError` is set; transport-level failures also throw a `FetchError`.

The `FetchError` message format is `[METHOD] "url": <status> <statusText> <message>`, and it lazily exposes `request`, `options`, `response`, `data`, `status`/`statusCode`, `statusText`/`statusMessage`.
Four lifecycle hooks are supported and may each be a single function or an array: onRequest, onRequestError, onResponse, onResponseError.
`baseURL` prefixes relative request URLs and `query`/`params` are merged with defaults and appended to the URL.
`$fetch.create(defaults, globalOptions)` produces a new client with deeply merged defaults for headers, query, and params.
`$fetch.native` exposes the underlying fetch implementation without any ofetch behavior.
The Node entry point keeps HTTP connections alive when the `FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE` environment variable parses to true.
Build uses unbuild with declaration output, dual CJS/ESM emission, and `undici` kept external.
Tests run on Vitest against a locally started h3 application (listhen) with endpoints for ok/params/url/echo/post/binary/403/408/204/timeout.
A dispatcher option (undici) is supported on Node 18+, with `agent` as the legacy alternative for older Node versions.
